findings.title: X-4 only partly fixed: other invisible format characters (U+2060, U+00AD, bidi U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069) count as visible and are accepted
findings.evidence: Ran the shipped NormalizeReason standalone: "\u2060\u2060\u2060" -> true, "\u00ad\u00ad\u00ad" -> true, "ab\u202ec" -> true. A reason can still be visually empty, and a bidi override (RLO) can make the audit_logs reason render reversed/spoofed in any viewer. Client mirror (ops-service.ts:361) has the same gap. Vietnamese NFC and NFD input (combining marks are Mn) is accepted, which is correct and must stay.
findings.fix: Treat the whole Cf category as invisible: use unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, c) instead of zeroWidth (do not count toward the 3, trim at edges), and optionally reject bidi controls U+202A..U+202E and U+2066..U+2069 outright. Mirror with /\p{Cf}/u on the client. Do not touch Mn/Mc so Vietnamese combining marks stay valid; add a test with an NFD Vietnamese reason (e.g. "Kha\u0302\u0309n") to lock that in.

findings.title: Client and server edge-trim sets differ for U+0085 (NEL)
findings.evidence: Go unicode.IsSpace includes U+0085, so the server trims "\u0085abc" and accepts it (verified). JS /\s/u does not include U+0085, which then hits \p{Cc} and the client rejects. The client is stricter, so this is only an inconsistency, not a bypass.
findings.fix: Add \u0085 to isEdgeBlank, or note the difference in the comment that says the rules match app.NormalizeReason.

findings.title: X-3 read-back failure still answers active:true with the submitted rate (not the stored value)
findings.evidence: On RateOverride error storedActive stays true and stored = rate, so the response echoes the request; only a WARN is logged. X-3 named both the concurrent-DELETE case (now fixed) and the failed read-back case. No test covers the read-error branch.
findings.fix: Either accept and document it in contracts ("on read-back failure the applied value is reported"), with a test pinning that behaviour, or do HSET + HGET in one Lua script/MULTI so the response always comes from Redis.

findings.title: Polling keeps running after a 401 while the sign-in prompt is shown
findings.evidence: Only 403 sets stoppedRef; LiveWarRoom renders SignInRequired on errorStatus 401 but the hook stays mounted and polls. No redirect loop (SignInRequired is a plain Link), and recovery after re-login in another tab is arguably useful, but each tick re-runs the auth path. The sales dashboard behaves the same.
findings.fix: Optional: stop polling on 401 like 403, or back off. Also consider passing a return-to parameter on the /auth/sign-in link.
